newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ roads still closed in aftermath of Fergus.
newsitem.headline: NZ roads still closed in aftermath of Fergus.

text.p: New Zealand authorities were reviewing road conditions as a clean-up operation began in the upper North Island after Monday's heavy storms.

Radio New Zealand reported queues of vehicles at road blocks in the Coromandel Peninsula, where heavy slips had caused havoc. The Automobile Association warned of delays as crews worked to reopen and repair roads.
State Highway 1 was closed south of Whangarei at the Brynderwyns because of a slip, and State Highway 2 was closed between Paeroa and Waihi at the Karangahape Gorge.
On the Coromandel, State Highway 25 was closed at Tairua and between Thames and Coromandel, and the Kopu-Hikuwai road was closed.
On the East Cape, Highway 35 at Tikitiki was closed by a bridge wash out.
MetService forecaster Augie Auer praised the public response to the remnants of Cyclone Fergus. "Without proper warnings, we could have lost half a dozen lives in this," he said.
The storm was now about 150 km east of Wellington and was petering out, wiht no further major rainfall threatened.
